Obonga: Project Update & Extension Agreement
Panther Metals PLC

, the exploration company focused on mineral projects in Canada, is pleased to provide an update for the Obonga Project ("Obonga" or the "Property"), which covers over 90% of the Obonga Greenstone Belt, in Ontario, Canada.

Preliminary findings from the Phase 1 Diamond Drilling programme at the Wishbone volcanogenic hosted massive sulphide ("VMS") prospect continue to strengthen our confidence in the scale and potential of this VMS system, with portable x-ray fluorescence ("pXRF") readings confirming the visual identification of copper minerals grading 8.34% copper in addition to the previously  reported zinc mineralisation (grading up to 11.65% Zn) intersected in the previous drilling campaigns at Wishbone.1

Considering the preliminary findings Panther have agreed a further extension of the Obonga sale and purchase agreement to facilitate drill permit renewals to allow for future infill drilling based on the anticipated results of the Phase 1 Diamond Drilling Programme which is due to continue with step-out drilling into 2027.
Darren Hazelwood, Chief Executive Officer commented:

"The latest work at Wishbone continues to strengthen our confidence in the scale and potential of this VMS system. The pXRF reading of 8.34% copper is particularly exciting because, alongside the high-grade zinc already identified at Wishbone, we are now seeing clear evidence of significant base-metal grade within the system.

This copper mineralisation also provides a compelling geological explanation for the very significant copper anomalies identified in the historic lake-sediment geochemistry surrounding Wishbone. We have known those anomalies were there; we are now beginning to see the mineralised system capable of producing them.

Importantly, this is not an isolated indicator. The lithologies, alteration, sulphides, geochemistry and mineralisation are all pointing in the same direction. We are seeing every ingredient we would expect from a substantial VMS system - and, critically, we are now seeing grade.
We have always believed we were right about Wishbone. The evidence continues to build around that conviction.

We now look forward to receiving the laboratory assays from the programme and getting back to drilling. Wishbone is a big system, and our job now is to determine just how big and how well mineralised it is."
Phase 1 Drill Programme Update

The Phase 1 Drill Programme drilling and access trail construction activities at Obonga were paused for a period during Canadian Government wildfire restrictions which impacted much of Northwestern Ontario this summer, with trail building resuming in the second half of August.

The drill core from the three holes drilled to date have been logged and analysed utilising a pXRF spectrometer.  In line with the Exploration Permit conditions the drilling activities have paused to accommodate the autumn hunting season and will resume this winter as accommodated by the Obonga extension agreements (announced 6 July 2026).2

The drill core from the summer drilling has been logged and photographed, with magnetic susceptibility readings and pXRF assays undertaken for the entire drill strings. The drill core is currently being processed, and laboratory assays are expected in due course.

Whilst the point-data pXRF readings cannot be considered representative of core intervals as grades can only be reliably determined through the chemical analysis of crushed core samples, they do provide a useful supplement to the identification of specific minerals observed in the drill core, as well as providing a guide to sample selection for laboratory assays and subsequent drill hole planning.

The pXRF readings at Wishbone have confirmed the visual identification of discrete chalcopyrite mineralisation containing up to 8.34% copper (see Figure 1), within a much wider intersection of pyrrhotite dominated massive sulphide and semi-massive sulphide mineralisation (reported 10 July 2026).3

This copper mineralisation is particularly significant as it is the first seen at this tenor in the Obonga drilling and provides compelling geological support for the existence of the expected much more extensive copper mineralisation that could be the source of the significant copper anomalies identified in the lake-sediment samples taken from Wishbone lake and the streams which drain off the Wishbone area both to the north and to the south (Figure 3).

An important characteristic of VMS deposits is that they typically display a zonation of metals within the massive sulphide body from Fe+Cu at the base to Zn+Fe±Pb±Ba at the top and margins, related to differing temperature and chemical conditions at mineral deposition. The major observed mineral component of the Wishbone massive sulphide mineralisation is pyrrhotite with less common pyrite and minor sphalerite and chalcopyrite in distinct zones.

The Wishbone access trail is nearing completion having successfully connected old logging trails via the Obonga West Road to the main road network to Thunder Bay (Figure 2). There is a short section of new trail still required to connect to the drill permit area in addition to further upgrading of the existing logging trails to facilitate year-round access.

Figure 1: Photograph of drill core with chalcopyrite mineralisation (gold coloured) which yielded pXRF readings of 8.34% Cu at 146.5m downhole depth in drill hole BR26-WB-P1-1. With the measurement screenshot from Olympus Vanta M Series pXRF unit
Figure 2: Section of Panther's new drill access trail linking the logging trails west of the Obonga West Road with logging trails in the Uneven Lake Area
Obonga Extension

By mutual agreement Panther and Broken Rock Resources Ltd ("Broken Rock") have agreed to a further extension amendment over Obonga.  The extension amendment to the 2021 sale and purchase agreement (the "Amendment Agreement") extends the terms of the original agreement (as announced 2 August 2021 and amended 6 July 2026), from the previous expiry date of 30 April 2027 to 31 August 2027.2,4

In light of the very positive preliminary findings of the Phase 1 Diamond Drilling programme at the Wishbone VMS prospect, and the drilling at the Awkward Conduit Target (announced 2 June 2026)5, the extension has been agreed to facilitate drill permit renewals to allow for future infill drilling based on the anticipated results of the Phase 1 Diamond Drilling Programme.

In consideration for the extension provided by the Amendment Agreement, the Company have issued share options to subscribe for 25,000 ordinary shares of no par value in the capital of the Company, at an exercise price of £1.70, over a three-year term expiring 31 August 2029. The share options issued under the 2021 sale and purchase agreement expired without exercise on 26 July 2026.

Obonga Project - Advancing a High-Impact VMS and Critical Minerals District

Panther Metals' Obonga Project in Ontario continues to demonstrate strong potential as a district-scale exploration opportunity targeting base and critical minerals. Since acquiring the Obonga Greenstone Belt in July 2021, the Company has advanced multiple high-priority targets including Wishbone, Awkward, Survey, Ottertooth, and Silver Rim.

On 9 February 2026 Panther announced plans for an approximately 2,000-metre diamond drilling program at the Wishbone Prospect, following the grant of an Exploration Permit in June 2024 valid through 2027. Previous work confirmed compelling VMS-style mineralisation, including 27.3m of massive sulphide and 51m of sulphide-dominated mineralisation across multiple lenses, supported by high-grade copper anomalies in lake sediments.

In July 2024, Panther secured an Exploration Permit for Awkward West, enabling up to 31 drill holes. Historic drilling returned 27.2m at 2.25% TGC, with zones exceeding 5% TGC, alongside indications of nickel, copper, and platinum group elements, aligning with the Company's critical minerals strategy.

High-resolution magnetic and electromagnetic surveys continue to refine drill targeting across Obonga. Survey and Ottertooth remain highly prospective, hosting multiple untested geophysical anomalies and historic massive sulphide intercepts.
Winston Project - Tailings Evaluation and MRE Pathway

Panther Metals' Winston Project represents a near-term, development-focused opportunity centred on the evaluation of historic mine tailings and has been the subject of prior technical and commercial assessment involving Extrakt.

Current work is focused on tailings sampling, metallurgical testing, and data validation to define metal content, recoverability, and support the preparation of a Mineral Resource Estimate (MRE). This approach provides a clear value-creation pathway with lower geological risk than greenfield exploration and aligns with modern reprocessing and critical mineral's themes.
Dotted Lake Project - Hemlo-Adjacent Polymetallic Opportunity
Panther Metals' Dotted Lake Project, acquired in July 2020, is located approximately 16km from Barrick Gold's Hemlo Mine, within a well-established mining region.

Early exploration identified multiple gold and base metal anomalies, with initial drilling confirming gold mineralisation. In early 2025, follow-up drilling materially advanced the project, confirming nickel and magnesium mineralisation within an ultramafic intrusion and identifying a VMS-style system, significantly expanding the project's polymetallic potential.
The program refined structural controls, extended mineralisation, and identified multiple new drill targets, positioning Dotted Lake as a high-upside, multi-commodity exploration asset.
Commercial Strategy - Focused Value Creation

Panther Metals is focused on disciplined, discovery-driven value creation through efficient capital deployment and technical execution. With Obonga delivering high-impact exploration, Winston providing a resource-focused development pathway, and Dotted Lake offering polymetallic upside, the Company maintains a balanced portfolio aligned with favourable commodity market conditions.
The Company's strategy is to advance high-quality assets along the most efficient technical pathway, delivering tangible milestones that underpin long-term shareholder value.
